findings.issue_text: [High/bug] CalendarService.ts:~95 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` result stores the entire Zod safeParse wrapper (`{ success, data, error }`) as the credential `key` instead of `.data`, corrupting stored credential shape for every Google Calendar token refresh

[High/bug] CalendarService.ts:~86 — In credential-sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` Response but code treats it as google-authlib result (`res?.data` → `token.access_token`); response body never parsed, so `access_token`/`expiry_date` are undefined and refresh flow is broken in sync mode

[High/bug] parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-9 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` does not create a dynamic catch-all key; both computed keys evaluate to the same literal string, intended validation never applied, and unknown keys (e.g. `expires_in`, `refresh_token`) are silently stripped by Zod default behavior — use `.passthrough()` or `z.record()` with refinement

[Medium/bug] hubspot CalendarService.ts:~177 — In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` Response assigned to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken`; reads of `refresh_token`/`expires_in` will be undefined since response body is never `await response.json()`-ed

[Medium/bug] zohocrm CalendarService.ts:~204 — `refreshOAuthTokens` can return a `fetch` Response but code accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` (axios-style shape); in sync mode `data` is undefined so the error check silently passes and empty token data is persisted

[Medium/bug] zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:~89 — Passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id as `calcomUserId`, likely causing sync failures or syncing another user's credentials

[Medium/security] app-credential.ts:25-28 — Webhook secret compared with `!==` (non-timing-safe); use constant-time comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to prevent timing attacks, and `req.headers[name]` can be `string[]` causing the comparison to always fail with a confusing 403

[Medium/security] app-credential.ts:62-70 — Decrypted `keys` payload is `JSON.parse`-ed and written straight into `credential.key` without validating against the app's credential schema (appMetadata fetched but never used for validation); malformed or malicious payload corrupts credential data and can break booking flows

[Medium/concurrency] app-credential.ts:60-86 — findFirst-then-create/update is racy: two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app can both see no existing credential and create duplicates; wrap in a transaction or add a unique constraint on (userId, appId) with an upsert

[Medium/bug] app-credential.ts:31,64 — `schema.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` can throw with no try/catch or method restriction, surfacing unhandled 500s (and GET requests with the header can trigger credential writes); return 400 on invalid input and check `req.method`

[Medium/data] parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 — Setting `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (a placeholder) and having callers persist the parsed result overwrites the real refresh token in the DB with a fake value; after sync mode is disabled those credentials can never be refreshed again

[Medium/performance] salesforce CalendarService.ts:75-97 — Token refresh is unconditional (not gated on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`), so every service instantiation makes an extra network round-trip to login.salesforce.com adding latency to all calendar operations; also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (empty on HTTP/2) — use `response.ok`

[Low/doc] .env.example:242-244 — Comment says encryption key 'must be 32 bytes for AES256' but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`, which generates 24 bytes (32 base64 chars); self-hosters following instructions will provision an invalid-length key

[Low/doc] .env.example:236 / app-credential.ts:26 — Header name 'should be in lowercase' but code never normalizes the env value; Node lowercases incoming header names, so an uppercase `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` silently breaks verification with no warning

[Low/bug] constants.ts:103-104 — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is typed as `string | undefined` (result of `&&`), not a boolean; works in truthiness checks but leaks an env-string-typed value as an exported flag — wrap in `Boolean(...)`

[Medium/test_gap] No tests added for the new webhook handler, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (especially the invalid dynamic-key schema), or `refreshOAuthTokens` sync/normal mode branching — the highest-risk paths in this PR are untested

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to define dynamic keys via computed properties `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS this does not create a catch-all/dynamic key; it evaluates to a single literal property name (stringified object), so it won’t validate real token fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date`. Also, since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default and the schema doesn’t use `.passthrough()`/`catchall`, any extra fields would be stripped rather than preserved. This is a concrete correctness defect in the diff-introduced schema/validation logic.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set and `userId` is truthy, the function returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response`. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, this return value is assigned to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` (line shown in diff) with no `await response.json()` conversion. That means in sync mode `hubspotRefreshToken` will be a `Response` object, not a `HubspotToken`, so downstream reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` / `hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in` (implied by the existing refresh-token update logic) will be `undefined` at runtime.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts` the code now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately uses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in this diff) returns a `fetch` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, and a `Response` does not have an axios-style `.data` field. So in sync mode this will break at runtime (accessing `undefined.error`), i.e., the refresh flow is incorrect given the return type introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app-credential.ts:25-28 — Webhook secret compared with `!==` (non-timing-safe); use constant-time comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to prevent timing attacks, and `req.headers[name]` can be `string[]` causing the comparison to always fail with a confusing 403

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook auth check directly compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next.js/Node, `req.headers[name]` can be `string | string[] | undefined`, so if multiple header values are present the comparison will always fail and return a 403 unexpectedly. Also, using `!==` for secret comparison is not constant-time, which is a security weakness for an auth secret check in a webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app-credential.ts:62-70 — Decrypted `keys` payload is `JSON.parse`-ed and written straight into `credential.key` without validating against the app's credential schema (appMetadata fetched but never used for validation); malformed or malicious payload corrupts credential data and can break booking flows

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` and immediately `JSON.parse`s it, then persists it directly into `prisma.credential.update/create({ data: { key: keys } })` with no validation of structure/types against any app-specific credential schema. Although `appMetadata` is fetched, it is only used for `slug/type`, not to validate `keys`. A malformed (or intentionally crafted) payload can therefore corrupt `credential.key`, which is later assumed to match per-app schemas elsewhere (e.g., calendar services using zod parsing), potentially breaking flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] app-credential.ts:60-86 — findFirst-then-create/update is racy: two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app can both see no existing credential and create duplicates; wrap in a transaction or add a unique constraint on (userId, appId) with an upsert

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a non-atomic `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }})` and then conditionally `create` vs `update`. With two concurrent webhook requests for the same `(userId, appId)`, both can observe no row and both proceed to `create`, which can lead to duplicate credentials (if no DB unique constraint) or a unique-constraint error/500 (if a constraint exists). The diff shows no transaction/upsert/unique enforcement here, so the race is real in the introduced logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc] .env.example:236 / app-credential.ts:26 — Header name 'should be in lowercase' but code never normalizes the env value; Node lowercases incoming header names, so an uppercase `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` silently breaks verification with no warning

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check indexes `req.headers` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` verbatim: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. Node/Next lowercases incoming header names in `req.headers`, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set to a non-lowercase value (common for header names), the lookup will miss and the check will fail, returning 403 even when the correct header is sent. The `.env.example` comment says it “should be in lowercase”, but the code does not enforce/normalize it or warn, so this is a real, diff-grounded broken-behavior risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] constants.ts:103-104 — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is typed as `string | undefined` (result of `&&`), not a boolean; works in truthiness checks but leaks an env-string-typed value as an exported flag — wrap in `Boolean(...)`

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which in TS evaluates to `string | undefined` rather than a boolean. The diff shows it being used in truthiness checks (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` and in `parseRefreshTokenResponse`/`refreshOAuthTokens`), so runtime behavior is fine, but exporting a non-boolean “_ENABLED” flag is a concrete API/type correctness issue that can confuse downstream consumers; wrapping with `Boolean(...)` would make the flag’s type and intent accurate.
